title: Sustainability in diagnostic and interventional endoscopy
summary:
Gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures require the use of numerous single-use devices and packaging materials, which generate substantial amounts of waste. At the same time, sustainability and responsible resource management are becoming increasingly important in healthcare. However, only limited data are currently available on the actual amount of consumables and packaging waste generated during endoscopic procedures.
The aim of this study is to systematically assess the use of single-use devices and the associated packaging waste during endoscopic procedures. To achieve this, a total of 1,000 endoscopic examinations will be evaluated. The materials used during each procedure will be documented using a digital recording system. In addition, all packaging materials will be collected and analyzed with regard to their weight in order to determine the relationship between packaging material and the actual medical product.
The results of this study are expected to identify opportunities for reducing waste and resource consumption and to support the development of strategies for more sustainable endoscopic practice. In the long term, the study aims to contribute to more environmentally sustainable and resource-efficient patient care.
